clue.text: Thus maiden entertained by youth is well-endowed

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being held within their company, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a youth is a boy
thus means so, as in 'do it so'
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl taken out by a young man turns out to be curvaceous.
explanation.definitionFit: Busty or full-chested is the sense, a figure with a generous bust.

clue.text: A dress lifted in Portuguese city

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting raises the letters, so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress

explanation.surface: A dress hitched up in a city in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: Braga is a large city in northern Portugal.

clue.text: Tail supporting pole, as strut

indicators.note: in a down entry the piece doing the supporting sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: S is the South Pole
a tail is a wagger, the thing that wags

explanation.surface: A tail on a pole as a structural prop.
explanation.definitionFit: To swagger is to walk with a conceited, swaying gait.

clue.text: Bones at times broken, including a radius

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bones that sometimes fracture, among them a forearm bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' turns AT TIMES into METATSI, and AR goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsals are the long bones of the foot.

clue.text: Union of creep and premier of supermodels — that's hard to understand

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: to creep is to crawl along slowly

explanation.surface: A sleazy hanger-on marrying a top model is a pairing nobody can make sense of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union of' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegible handwriting is a mess of letters that is difficult to read or decipher.

clue.text: Gripper, mollusc stuck on bottom of ship

parts.note: a clam is a mollusc

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A shellfish clinging to a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A clamp is a tool for holding things tightly in place.

clue.text: Lots here fighting to rescue university

indicators.note: rescuing someone means gathering them in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: fighting is action, as in seeing action

explanation.surface: Plenty of fighting going on to save a university.
explanation.definitionFit: At a sale by bidding, items are offered as numbered lots.

clue.text: Rake leaves out in ideal amounts, tidied up

indicators.note: tidying up means rearranging, so the remaining letters are reordered
leaves means abandons, so the word that follows is taken away

explanation.surface: Raking fallen leaves into neat piles in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes O, U, T from IDEAL AMOUNTS, giving IDEALAMNS, which 'tidied up' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a womaniser, a man who chases and charms women.

clue.text: Players holding an ace then, for a game of cards

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast
A is the usual abbreviation for an ace on playing cards

explanation.surface: Card players clutching an ace, settling in for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' just puts A after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: Retail lines putting fish in plain packaging?

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: plain means bare, unadorned
a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Wrapping fish in unbranded paper, as at a fishmonger's counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The striped code scanned at a till is a set of printed lines used in shops.

clue.text: Delicate creature finding Spooner's drinking vessel empty?

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds of the two pieces trade places

parts.note: a flagon is a large drinking vessel
an empty glass is dry

explanation.surface: A drained flagon prompting a tipsy spoonerism.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-bodied insect with fine, gauzy wings.

clue.text: Noted aggressive performance of a no-good idol into crack

indicators.note: into says the pieces before it go inside the following one

parts.note: a crack is a gap
NG is a common abbreviation for no good
an idol is a star

explanation.surface: A worthless pop idol breaking into the big time gives a combative show.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Noted' means set to music; this hip-hop style is known for its confrontational lyrics.

clue.text: On the contrary, police inspector's lead provides a piece of information

indicators.note: on the contrary suggests turning things the other way round, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: a lead goes first, so only the opening letter of inspector is taken

explanation.surface: A police inspector's lead turns out to be a useful clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single entry or detail, such as a news story or a fact in a list.

clue.text: Less likely to get runs in the end when sent back

indicators.note: being sent back means returning the way it came, so the letters are read backwards
in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the end of something is its rear
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman less likely to score runs at the end of the innings once returned to the pavilion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rarer is less common, so less likely to happen.

clue.text: Old African or Danish translated around English

indicators.note: around says one piece is placed about the other
translated means changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Danish text rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' turns OR DANISH into RHODSIAN, and E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe, so this is a dated term for one of its people.

clue.text: On manoeuvres, more go in for a battle cry

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres are moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers on exercises charge further in, yelling for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Paratroopers famously shout it as they jump; it is a cry of bold attack.

clue.text: Equip mother with part for song and dance

parts.note: to rig is to equip, as with a ship
ma is mother
a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: Kitting out mum with a role in a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean a long, fussy fuss and bother, a tediously elaborate procedure.

clue.text: African, very African

parts.note: very means so, as in 'so good'
someone from Mali in West Africa is Malian

explanation.surface: A person described as African, and emphatically so.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Somalia, in the Horn of Africa, is African.

clue.text: Sneeze in the general direction of children, audibly

indicators.note: audibly says we want what the words sound like rather than how they are written

parts.words: in the general direction of children
parts.note: aiming at your offspring is at, towards, your issue, meaning children

explanation.surface: Sneezing towards the kids, loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: The British imitation of the noise a sneeze makes.

clue.text: African country unable to carry things back?

parts.note: someone with no bag has nothing to carry things in

explanation.surface: A country whose people are too poor to carry belongings home.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a nation on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa.

clue.text: Fight to control Mini in sudden loss of a tyre

indicators.note: controlling something means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bout is a fight, as in boxing
mini means small or short, so low

explanation.surface: Struggling to keep a Mini car on the road after a tyre bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre that bursts suddenly while driving is said to have this.

clue.text: Fairy doing the backstroke in Yorkshire pudding

indicators.note: doing the backstroke says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the hidden stretch; IREP from 'YorkshIRE Pudding', read backwards.

clue.text: Call girl hosting party, a poisonous thing

parts.note: to give someone a bell is to phone them

indicators.note: hosting means having guests inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A call girl throwing a party turns out to be dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade is a highly toxic plant.

clue.text: Not entirely lacking sense, one making Russian food

indicators.note: not entirely means one short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: someone blind lacks the sense of sight
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A not-quite-senseless person cooking a Russian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Small buckwheat pancakes eaten in Russia, often with caviar.

clue.text: African country on the drink after uprising

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising means the letters climb, read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means on, concerning
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A nation drinking heavily after a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked state in West Africa.

clue.text: Fixture coming up that's put on late

parts.note: something coming up is near, or nigh
a sports fixture is a tie, a scheduled match

explanation.surface: A sports fixture approaching that is scheduled for a late kick-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is worn at bedtime, put on late in the day.

clue.text: Queens, perhaps, keeping gold in branch

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bough is a branch of a tree
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Royal women keeping their gold in a branch office of a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Queens is one of the five administrative districts of New York City, an example of the type.

clue.text: No thumbs up, that is, for relations

parts.note: a thumbs up signals approval, OK
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone refusing approval for family members.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang word for sex, so 'relations' in the sense of sexual relations.

clue.text: Man caught terrorising head, or bully

parts.note: he stands for any man
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man arrested for terrorising the headteacher, or some other bully.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to intimidate or browbeat someone.
